feedback: No race evidence exists yet (iteration 0 is the baseline), so these points come from what the controller had to handle, not from measured outcomes. Integration observation: with 12 mm footprints on a 2 cm pitch and a 25 mm tape, a centred line falls almost entirely on the middle sensor, and the outer sensors only start reading once the line moves about 1 cm off centre. This means the signal is small near centre and the controller has to use large weights (±2) at the outer sensors to get a usable response. Overall, the array's width and forward offset are the main things that will decide whether the robot can hold the line through bends, so the next race is the key test of that. If the next race shows many line-loss events or large rms_error on the slalom (the array is too narrow or too far from the wheels), widen the outer sensors and/or move the array forward. If it shows completion with steady error but the robot oscillates, the array is probably fine and the issue is the wheel track or mass limiting turn authority, so keep the geometry and adjust the mass or track instead. The sensor noise may also be large compared with the signal near centre, which would make tuning harder; check steering_oscillation against control_effort to see whether that is happening.
requested_changes: If the next race shows line_loss_events above zero on the slalom or rms_error above about 0.03: widen the outer sensors to x = ±0.03 (or ±0.04 with sensor_size 0.016) so the array keeps the line through sharp bends. Evidence basis: contract reading geometry only; no race yet.

If the next race completes with low rms_error but steering_oscillation is high: reduce the body mass toward 0.5 kg or keep the array and reduce wheel_track toward 0.10 m to lower yaw inertia. Evidence basis: contract physics (yaw inertia = mass*(L^2+W^2)/12); no race yet.
If the next race shows the line leaving the array on tight bends: move the sensor row forward to y = 0.06 so it reacts earlier than the wheels. Evidence basis: contract sensing geometry; no race yet.
